content: 1. The comparison between remdesivir and standard of care (SOC) or placebo for COVID-19 treatment was analyzed across multiple outcomes and subgroups. 2. For all-cause mortality, data from 10 studies involving 12,273 participants showed a risk ratio (RR) of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.84 to 1.01), indicating no statistically significant reduction in mortality with remdesivir compared to SOC or placebo. 3. In patients with mild to moderate disease, the risk ratio for all-cause mortality was 0.85 (95% CI: 0.57 to 1.27), while for those with severe to critical disease, the risk ratio was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.85 to 1.02). Neither subgroup demonstrated a statistically significant benefit. 4. Regarding the new need for mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the risk ratio for patients with mild to moderate disease was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.54 to 1.65), for severe to critical disease was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.47 to 1.15), and for moderate to severe disease was 0.57 (95% CI: 0.42 to 0.79). The latter subgroup showed a statistically significant reduction in the need for mechanical ventilation or ECMO with remdesivir. 5. Clinical improvement was assessed, with a risk ratio of 1.08 (95% CI: 1.03 to 1.13) for mild to moderate disease and 1.08 (95% CI: 1.02 to 1.14) for severe to critical disease, indicating a statistically significant improvement in both subgroups. 6. Serious adverse events were analyzed, with a risk ratio of 1.10 (95% CI: 1.01 to 1.19) for mild to moderate disease, suggesting a slight increase in adverse events with remdesivir. For severe to critical disease, the risk ratio was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.59 to 1.01), showing no statistically significant difference. 7. Hospital discharge rates were higher with remdesivir, with a risk ratio of 0.47 (95% CI: 0.29 to 0.74) for mild to moderate disease and 0.91 (95% CI: 0.72 to 1.14) for severe to critical disease. The benefit was statistically significant in the mild to moderate subgroup. 8. Hospitalization or death outcomes showed a risk ratio of 1.07 (95% CI: 1.00 to 1.14) for mild to moderate disease and 1.08 (95% CI: 1.01 to 1.16) for severe to critical disease, indicating a slight but statistically significant increase in this combined outcome with remdesivir. 9. For the subgroup analysis of hospitalization or death in patients with severe disease, the risk ratio was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.83 to 1.16), showing no significant difference. 10. The risk ratio for hospitalization or death in patients with mild to moderate disease was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.03 to 0.59), indicating a statistically significant reduction in this outcome with remdesivir. These findings were analyzed using the Review Manager software (version 5.4.1).
